Thank you. Good afternoon, Chair, Mayor, and members of Council. My name is Eric Schneider, and I'm a senior planner at the City.
I'm here today to make a recommendation for approval of a zoning bylaw amendment to permit a crematorium use in conjunction with a funeral home.
As we advance to the next slide, I will first discuss the site context of the lands.
The site is municipally addressed as 1014 Victoria Street North and is located on the north side of Victoria Street between Frederick Street and River Road.
The subject lands back onto an existing railway corridor regulated by Metrolinx.
The surrounding lands contain commercial and arterial commercial uses.
Access to Highway 7-8 is approximately 800 meters west of the subject lands.

The site and the building are currently undergoing renovation and associated site works to the parking lot, the building, and the landscaped areas to convert the site, a former home hardware store, into a funeral home.
On the next slide, I will discuss the proposed concept.
The funeral home use is currently permitted as of right in the zoning bylaw.
The applicant has obtained site plan approval to convert the site into the funeral home use.
The existing building and parking area will undergo slight modifications, including a new canopy at the front of the building, as shown in the rendering on the front facade.
The subject zoning bylaw amendment application proposes to add the use of crematorium in conjunction with the existing funeral home use.
The next slide illustrates the proposed Zoning By-law amendment.
The existing COMM-2 General Commercial Zone would remain.
The amendment would add a site-specific provision that permits the use of crematorium provided
it is set back a minimum of 80 metres from residential lands.
Next, I will briefly summarize the opportunity with this application.
To permit the redevelopment of the lands and the reuse of the site and the building.
To establish and provide an appropriate buffer to residential lands.
And to support a strong and robust economy in the commercial area of the Victoria North
community.
